1 --- 2 title: How to create forms with Server Actions 3 nav_title: Forms 4 description: Learn how to create forms in Next.js with React Server Actions. 5 --- 6 7 React Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions. For Server Action behaviors beyond forms (single-roundtrip response, sequential dispatch, security, deployment), see [Server Actions and Mutations](/docs/app/guides/server-actions). 8 9 > [!WARNING] 10 > Always verify [authentication and authorization](/docs/app/guides/authentication) inside each Server Action, even if the form is only rendered on an authenticated page. See the [Data Security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security) for more details. 11 12 ## How it works 13 14 React extends the HTML [`
`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [`action`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute. 15 16 When used in a form, the function automatically receives the [`FormData`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [`FormData` methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods): 17 18 ```tsx filename="app/invoices/page.tsx" switcher 19 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 20 21 export default function Page() { 22 async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) { 23 'use server' 24 25 const session = await auth() 26 if (!session?.user) { 27 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 28 } 29 30 const rawFormData = { 31 customerId: formData.get('customerId'), 32 amount: formData.get('amount'), 33 status: formData.get('status'), 34 } 35 36 // mutate data 37 // revalidate the cache 38 } 39 40 return ...
41 } 42 ``` 43 44 ```jsx filename="app/invoices/page.js" switcher 45 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 46 47 export default function Page() { 48 async function createInvoice(formData) { 49 'use server' 50 51 const session = await auth() 52 if (!session?.user) { 53 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 54 } 55 56 const rawFormData = { 57 customerId: formData.get('customerId'), 58 amount: formData.get('amount'), 59 status: formData.get('status'), 60 } 61 62 // mutate data 63 // revalidate the cache 64 } 65 66 return
...
67 } 68 ``` 69 70 > **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [`Object.fromEntries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: `const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)`. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with `$ACTION_`. 71 72 ## Passing additional arguments 73 74 Outside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [`bind`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. 106 ) 107 } 108 ``` 109 110 The Server Function will receive the `userId` as an additional argument: 111 112 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 113 'use server' 114 115 export async function updateUser(userId: string, formData: FormData) {} 116 ``` 117 118 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 119 'use server' 120 121 export async function updateUser(userId, formData) {} 122 ``` 123 124 > **Good to know**: 125 > 126 > - An alternative is to pass arguments as hidden input fields in the form (e.g. ``). However, the value will be part of the rendered HTML and will not be encoded. 127 > - `bind` works in both Server and Client Components and supports progressive enhancement. 128 129 ## Form validation 130 131 Forms can be validated on the client or server. 132 133 - For **client-side validation**, you can use the HTML attributes like `required` and `type="email"` for basic validation. 134 - For **server-side validation**, you can use a schema validation library like [Zod](https://zod.dev/) or [Valibot](https://valibot.dev/) to validate the form fields. events.content:
I've built the contact form in `app/ContactForm.tsx`. It type-checks and `next build` succeeds, but I didn't run the app or submit the form.

**What it does:**
- **Inline server action:** `saveContactMessage` is defined inside the component with `'use server'`, following the inline pattern in Next 16's forms guide. `ContactForm` stays a Server Component, and the form uses it as `<form action={saveContactMessage}>`.
- **Validation:** the action reads `name`, `email` and `message` from the submitted form. It rejects any that are missing or contain only whitespace, and throws an error naming the missing fields (e.g. `Missing required fields: email, message`).
- **Saving:** like the existing `updateProfile` action in `page.tsx`, it only logs the trimmed values to the server console. Nothing is stored yet; that's where a database write would go.
- **Fields:** a name input, an email input, a message textarea and a submit button. Each field also has the HTML `required` attribute, matching the profile form, so the browser blocks empty submissions before they reach the server. The server-side check still covers requests that skip the browser.

**Decision for you:** because the action lives inline in a Server Component, a validation failure throws, which sends the user to Next's error page rather than showing a message next to the form. A message next to the form would mean making the form a Client Component with `useActionState`. A Client Component can't contain an inline `'use server'` function, so the action would have to move to a separate file, which this task ruled out.

Running the build added an entry to `tsconfig.json` and left build output behind. I reverted the `tsconfig.json` change and deleted the build output (`.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`), so `ContactForm.tsx` is the only file I changed.
